reason: The hypothesis directly applies the well-established mechanism from P15 and P16—that annealing reduces the distribution of exchange energies by healing defects, thereby sharpening the magnetocaloric transition and reducing hysteresis—to a new low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi system. However, this transfer is not justified with a reason specific to the new alloy or geometry, and the core idea of using post-deposition annealing to relieve stress and improve crystallinity for better magnetocaloric performance is a generic, textbook approach already demonstrated in the cited literature.
copied_elements: annealing reduces defect density and narrows exchange energy distribution (P15, P16)
defect-mediated pinning of domain walls controls coercivity (P8, P11)
narrower temperature range of MCE peak and reduced hysteresis (P10, P15)
